Deep sleep %1$s of the %2$s since boot
Booted less than 30 minutes ago: too early to judge standby.
The phone is on external power: with USB or adb connected many phones never suspend (USB and charger wakelocks). Run the guided test unplugged.
Nothing reached deep sleep since boot: a wakelock or kernel wakeup source is held all the time, or every suspend attempt aborts (see suspend statistics and wakeup sources).
SELinux hides /sys/power from apps on this build; nothing wrong by itself.
/sys/power/state lists neither mem nor freeze: the kernel is built without CONFIG_SUSPEND or the platform PM driver did not register.
mem_sleep offers only s2idle: the SoC never enters its real low power state (PSCI / platform suspend ops missing), standby drains faster.
/sys/power/autosleep is \"%1$s\": the kernel suspends on its own instead of system_suspend, unusual on Android.
/sys/power/suspend_stats needs a newer kernel; on older kernels the statistics live only in debugfs, which this app never reads.
Suspend aborts often. Last failing device %1$s (errno %2$s, step %3$s): its suspend callback refuses, usually a driver with pending work or a busy IRQ.
The kernel never completed a suspend since boot.
Kernel and userspace wakelocks seen by the kernel

/sys/class/wakeup needs kernel 4.19 or later (or a backport) and may be blocked by SELinux; older kernels expose wakeup sources only in debugfs, which this app never reads. With DUMP granted, the wake locks check shows the framework side.
Held for a long time: %1$s. A driver keeps the system awake (stuck wake IRQ, modem or Wi-Fi wakelock, sensor hub).
Held for a long time: %1$s. External power is connected, which often holds such sources; check again on battery.
The thermal HAL reports severe heat: the device throttles and the measurements here are not representative.
Deep doze enabled, light doze disabled
config_enableAutoPowerModes is false (the AOSP default): apps are never put into doze and standby drains. Set it to true in the device framework overlay.
Grant DUMP from a PC (see Settings) to read it from dumpsys.
The guided test needs exact alarms: allow them in Settings, Apps, Special app access, Alarms & reminders.
Deep sleep is the gap between the elapsed and the awake clock
External power is connected: many phones do not suspend while charging over USB.
Does the phone sleep with the screen off, and does an alarm wake it on time?
1. Unplug the USB cable (adb keeps many phones awake).
2. Press the power button to turn the screen off.

plurals.name: suspend_test_step3
plurals.item: 3. Leave the phone alone for %1$d minute: an alarm wakes it at the end, the screen may stay off.
3. Leave the phone alone for %1$d minutes: an alarm wakes it at the end, the screen may stay off.

resources.string: 4. Come back to this screen: the results are computed automatically.
Waiting for the alarm; if it never arrives the test is evaluated two minutes after the due time.
External power was connected during the test, which often prevents suspend. Repeat on battery.
Partly awake: a wakelock or frequent wakeups interrupt deep sleep. Look at the wakeup sources and last_resume_reason.
With the screen off and on battery the kernel never suspended: a wakelock is held (dumpsys power, wakeup sources) or every suspend attempt aborts (a driver refusing suspend).
Alarm fired %1$s s after the due time
The wake-up came late: doze deferral or a slow resume (a driver taking long in its resume callback).
The RTC wake alarm did not wake the SoC: the phone woke for another reason later. Check that the RTC driver (e.g. rtc-pm8xxx) is a wakeup source and that the alarm IRQ is enabled for wake.
The exact alarm did not arrive within two minutes of its due time: the RTC alarm cannot wake the device from suspend (alarmtimer/RTC wake IRQ), or the app was force-stopped.
The phone hardly slept, so this does not prove wake-up from suspend.
Stopped before the alarm was due
A partial wakelock must keep the CPU running with the screen off

plurals.name: suspend_wl_hint
plurals.item: Hold the wakelock, turn the screen off for a minute or more, then come back and release it. While it is held the awake clock must keep pace with the elapsed one. It is released automatically after %1$d minute or when you leave this screen.

resources.string: The screen stayed on, which keeps the phone awake anyway: turn it off for at least 20 s while the wakelock is held.
CPU stayed awake for %1$s with the screen off
The kernel suspended while a partial wakelock was held: the framework wakelock does not reach the kernel (system_suspend, /sys/power/wake_lock permissions or SELinux).
